Q: Selecting a range of poker hands from a matrix A:

You're not overthinking it—most poker range charts aren't generated by a simple weighting formula. They're typically based on precomputed hand rankings derived from equity calculations, simulations, or GTO solver outputs. The slider simply includes the top X% of hand combinations from that ordered list (remembering that pairs have 6 combos, suited hands 4, and offsuit hands 12).

If you're looking to understand and practice these ranges instead of building them from scratch, Runout Poker provides free preflop range charts and AI-powered training to help you learn position-based ranges and make stronger preflop decisions.
https://apps.apple.com/us/app/runout-poker-trainer-gto-coach/id6760210288

Q: Relate two tables, one table has no data yet A:

The error column argument cannot be null means one of the DataColumn references you're passing is Nothing. This happens when the column name doesn't exist in the table's Columns collection.

It doesn't have anything to do with the table being empty. A DataRelation is based on the schema, so an empty table works fine as long as the columns are defined. While DACom.Fill usually builds the schema from the result set, I'd check if the query is actually returning the columns you expect.

You can manually ensure the columns exist before creating the relation:

' Ensure the Comments table has the expected columns
With DS.Tables("Comments").Columns
    If Not .Contains("JobID")      Then .Add("JobID",      GetType(Integer))
    If Not .Contains("EmpID")      Then .Add("EmpID",      GetType(Integer))
    If Not .Contains("MinRepDate") Then .Add("MinRepDate", GetType(DateTime))
    If Not .Contains("MaxRepDate") Then .Add("MaxRepDate", GetType(DateTime))
End With

Dim ParentCols() As DataColumn = {DS.Tables("Time").Columns("JobID"), DS.Tables("Time").Columns("EmpID"),
    DS.Tables("Time").Columns("MinRepDate"), DS.Tables("Time").Columns("MaxRepDate")}
Dim ChildCols() As DataColumn = {DS.Tables("Comments").Columns("JobID"), DS.Tables("Comments").Columns("EmpID"),
    DS.Tables("Comments").Columns("MinRepDate"), DS.Tables("Comments").Columns("MaxRepDate")}
Dim ComRel As New DataRelation("RCom", ParentCols, ChildCols)
DS.Relations.Add(ComRel)

But a SQL JOIN would just flatten these into one result. That's not the same as a parent-child relationship in memory. Once the columns exist, calling GetChildRows on a Time row will just return an empty array if there aren't any related Comments rows.

Q: Android Studio Gradle Sync fails with SocketTimeoutException downloading Gradle 8.13 A:

Android Studio's Gradle wrapper runs in a Java process that doesn't always pick up your system network configuration. Because the download timeout is hardcoded, you can't just bump it in gradle.properties.

Since you have the zip file already, I'd just point the wrapper at it. Change the distributionUrl in gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties to this:

distributionUrl=file:///C:/Users/YourName/Downloads/gradle-8.13-bin.zip

Delete the partial downloads in %USERPROFILE%\.gradle\wrapper\dists and sync. So if it's a network issue specific to the JVM, this local path bypasses the download entirely.

To see the logs, you can run gradlew --debug from the project root. It'll use the same JDK Android Studio uses.

Q: Is fetching std::chrono::steady_clock inside a critical section necessary to theoretically align C++ happens-before with real-time order? A:

You either have:

  • "clear", "empty" (the more natural case)
  • "ok", "clear" (the "inverted" execution)

Over a noticeable physical time gap (such as 1 hour), physical reality dictates t1 < t2.

Your timing seems huge, but you can also imagine a very slow machine with instructions which can take years to execute.

Waiting 1 year, 1h, 1s, 1ms is similar from the abstract machine.

And once you consider more "practical" cases, you are no longer in the theory.
